en: At that time, when the King of Gods Maheśvara, the Great Sovereign, was performing the ritual recitation of the dharma-nature of the celestial maidens of supernatural arts born through transformation,
the King of Gods Maheśvara was together with all the gods in the realm of Maheśvara.
Surrounded by women before and behind her,
she sported with supernatural powers and performed various musical performances.
Suddenly, from the parting of her hair, a celestial maiden manifested.
His countenance was upright and handsome, and his artistic skills were foremost;
among all the devas, none could surpass him.
In the midst of the great assembly, he spoke these words:
Now, for the sake of benefiting all,
whatever prayers I make for matters of abundance, auspiciousness,
and prosperity shall all be fulfilled according to my heart's desires.
One will swiftly achieve mastery in all crafts and arts.
I possess a secret dhāraṇī method;
I shall now proclaim it. Thus, he spoke the dhāraṇī:
*Namo uṃcīmāveśakṛtiprabhājihva karālīṃ tārāṃ śvajaṭile vīramajarīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* At that time, the goddesses of various arts and skills...
Having spoken this dhāraṇī,
he addressed the assembly of devas:
"If any among you wish to recite and uphold this dhāraṇī of mine..."
First, one must establish a *maṇḍala* and adorn it according to the Dharma,
making offerings of various incenses and flowers.
This should be done for either two weeks or one week.
Observe the fast and precepts, renounce sexual desire,
and recite this dhāraṇī ten thousand or one hundred thousand times. During that interval,
do not consume alcohol, meat, or anything foul-smelling or defiling.
If one recites and maintains this with a sincere heart, the goddess will appear before them and provide all manner of empowerments;
all aspirations and requests shall be completely fulfilled,
and from that time forward, there will be no further obstacles.
Even if one's wife and children are defiled by impurities,
they shall not be restrained or severed;
if one can maintain purity, this will yield the most rapid efficacy.
Whatever is to be used hereafter should be brought to accomplishment.
When performing the recitation, one must first perform the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
Either water or ash should be empowered by reciting [the mantra] seven times.
Sprinkle [the water] in the four directions according to the desired distance;
it will immediately constitute a consecrated boundary (sīmābandha), such that no ghosts or spirits can approach.
If one recites it up to one thousand times,
it will cause devas, nāgas, humans, and non-humans to see it and immediately rejoice.
If one recites it up to two thousand times, [the same result follows].
All ghosts and spirits shall provide protection and guardianship.
If one recites it three thousand times,
the spirits of medicinal herbs will all manifest before one.
The deities of the flower and fruit forests will joyfully follow one;
if one recites it four thousand times,
all the vaitaraṇa spirits will develop profound reverence.
If one recites it five thousand times,
all the dragon spirits and their retinues— both male and female— will rejoice, look up with reverence, and cherish it without weariness.
If one recites it six thousand times, [the same shall occur].
All the male and female yakṣa retinues will joyfully follow him and serve at his command.
If one recites this seven thousand times, [the result will be attained].
All the celestial kings, such as Mādhāru and others,
together with their retinues, attend upon him,
performing various services and labors without ever growing weary.
If one recites it up to eight thousand times,
all the vidyādharas, rishis possessing the five supernatural powers,
and others will give rise to profound joy and look up to it with inexhaustible reverence.
If one recites it ten thousand times,
or even up to one hundred thousand times,
all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth [will be subdued].
Even unto the gods of the Sāṃkāśya heaven and all the spirits and deities,
they will give rise to great joy, following and guarding the practitioner,
constantly ensuring their abundance and auspiciousness.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to pray for the cessation [of calamity], it shall not be difficult.
When there is a drought, one should construct a ritual boundary (*sīmābandha*) and altar according to the rules, perform *homa* offerings, and recite this mantra ten thousand times.
The rain will fall at the appropriate time.
If the rain becomes excessive and one wishes it to cease,
one should empower pure ashes one hundred and eight times with mantras.
If one hurls it into the air, the rain will immediately cease.
Furthermore, if there is an enemy who gives rise to malicious intent,
one may use vermilion or red earth.
Whether it be the name of the book or its physical form,
one should step upon it with the left foot while reciting the mantra.
This should be performed one hundred and eight times after nightfall.
Regardless of whether they are far or near, those enemies will come of their own accord to seek the resolution of their enmity;
their minds will become harmonious and compliant, and they will further give rise to affection and reverence.
Furthermore, regarding the method for wishing to employ all ghosts and spirits:
One should gather them all together and give rise to a heart of compassion; then,
empower the food and drink according to one's means by reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times,
and distribute it as an offering.
Thereafter, they shall be swiftly driven to accomplish [the task];
they will constantly give rise to joy and never depart from the person.
Furthermore, as for the method: if one wishes to summon all people, [one should proceed as follows].
Whatever comes to mind, regardless of distance,
empower water seven times and scatter it in the four directions while looking toward that person and reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times.
Whether they recognize him or not,
they all come running to him and follow whatever his mind commands, not daring to disobey.
Furthermore, if there should be an enemy who comes wishing to cause him harm, [the mantra protects him].
Recite the vidyā with a sincere mind one hundred and eight times;
his body will then be struck by a seal of fire.
If he turns his mind and submits, he shall be subdued.
At the time of releasing [the patient],
recite the vidyā seven times and say, "Release!
Immediately, their body will be restored to its original state.
Furthermore, there is another method: if there are husband and wife whose outward hearts are at odds and who do not take pleasure in seeing one another,
being as mutually hostile as fire and water;
Secretly write down their names so that they remain unaware;
then, following the previous ritual exactly, step upon them with the left foot while reciting the name one thousand and eight times.
They immediately became harmonious and compliant, loving one another as if they were glue and lacquer;
they never again gave rise to thoughts of hatred or betrayal.
Furthermore, according to the Dharma, if there is someone whom one loves, one should proclaim it to one's wife.
Even the celestial maidens, court ladies, and the consorts and retinues of Śakra, Lord of Devas— whomever the heart desires—
one shall summon them by reciting according to the aforementioned method.
At that moment, they will arrive spontaneously, seeking him out and requesting to serve as attendants.
If one does not violate [the precepts], one will never be abandoned by them.
Furthermore, regarding the method for summoning yakṣiṇīs and others:
if one desires to seek their wealth and treasures, one may summon them at will according to one's heart's desire.
They arrived with great speed.
They offered everything they required and requested to become his wives, concubines, or attendants.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to gain the love and respect of all noble persons,
one should recite the name [of the deity] one thousand and eight times;
they will then come of their own accord to pay homage and serve as one's attendants.
Furthermore, if one enters a government office,
one should recite this vidyā seven times with a sincere mind upon arrival;
looking up toward auspicious signs from afar, one shall cause all matters to accord with one's wishes.
If one sees his face, one experiences immeasurable joy;
if there is a matter to request, he will surely act on one's behalf.
Furthermore, according to another method, if there is a woman one loves:
Alternatively, for a man whose mind is inclined toward pleasure,
one should empower either *kunkuma* or the juice of red-blue flowers and smear it beneath the soles of his two feet.
Heat it over a fire and cover it with both hands;
while reciting the mantra and calling their name, they will immediately arrive,
coming of their own accord to seek you out even in the most secluded places.

When directly approaching to see [the deity] and so forth until the end of one's life, do not consent to abandon [the practice]; whenever reciting the name, add the syllable *sa-bha-ha* above it, excluding the two syllables *phaṭ*.
If it is a woman seeking a man, she should perform the rite according to the previous method, and he will arrive immediately according to her wish.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to cause the bodies of various ghosts and spirits to appear, [she should likewise perform the rite].
Take firewood from a *śītavana* (charnel ground) where dead persons are cremated;
perform the *homa* by burning one piece of wood for each recitation of the mantra,
continuing until one hundred and eight repetitions are completed.
All ghosts and spirits will manifest their own forms so that one may see them face to face.
Furthermore, regarding all manner of wealth and treasures,
if one recites this with a sincere heart according to whatever one requires, they will be naturally obtained.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to bind a person and question them about their affairs—
regardless of whether they are high or low, pure or impure—
one should visualize the Honored One (the deity) and recite the mantra with a sincere mind.
Immediately upon binding him, he questioned him and came to know the matters of the three periods of time;
he explained everything such that there was nothing he did not know.
It was not merely that he could bind a single person.
Even if as many as hundreds of thousands of people recite this with a sincere heart,
they will be bound simultaneously according to their thoughts and intentions.
Furthermore, if there is a family member who has run away and gone to a very distant place, [one may employ this method].
Step upon it while reciting the name as prescribed in the preceding letter;
the person will return and arrive in a state of hurried flight.
If they are late in coming, immediately write their form in ash.
Perform the ritual three times each day.
Strike [the bell] once for every recitation of the mantra,
continuing from one strike up to twenty-one recitations.
He will immediately become terrified, like a wind that has suddenly arrived.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cure all diseases,
one should take khadira wood.
Cut it into twenty-one pieces.
Recite the vidyā-mantra once for each piece and cast them into the fire until all have been burned.
Once this is completed, any illness whatsoever shall be cured.
Furthermore, according to another method, if there is one suffering from a spirit-induced illness,
take asafoetida, agallochum, realgar, white mustard seeds, eaglewood, or *lianye* (Cinnamomum tamala) leaves, and so forth;
grind them together into a paste and form forty-nine pills.
Recite the mantra once and cast it once into the fire, and the illness will be cured immediately. Furthermore,
for those suffering from the affliction of *huxue* (fox-demon) possession,
take realgar, white mustard seeds, *khuṅ-khiung*, single-headed *qiu*, rhinoceros horn, the urine of a black ram, the dewclaws of a white horse, and the "night-eye" of a donkey or horse.
Grind and sift [the ingredients] together to form pills.
Empower them one hundred and eight times by reciting the mantra over them,
then burn them to fumigate within the nostrils.
If one also applies [this] to the body, the fox-spirits will be extinguished and the illness will immediately be cured.
All the beneficial methods described above are divinely efficacious and will be swiftly accomplished.
In all cases where one wishes to perform a rite, it must be done with utmost sincerity.
If one lacks a sincere mind and recites with negligence or disrespect, it will be of no benefit and the rite will not be accomplished.
If performed with a sincere heart, efficacy will be obtained even after a single recitation.
I have now briefly explained only a small portion;
other dharmas cannot be fully exhausted.
If you wish to maintain this recitation and seek its spiritual efficacy, [you should do so].
First, draw my mandala and paint my image and install it within the mandala.
By making offerings according to the ritual, one will swiftly obtain signs of efficacy and swiftly achieve accomplishment.
Regarding the method for painting the image: for the image of the Great Sovereign Goddess (Maheśvarī), first paint the Heavenly King Maheśvara.
He has three faces and six arms, with a countenance that is extraordinary, upright, and formidable.
From the hairline of his head, a celestial maiden is miraculously born;
she is exquisite and lovely, such that none in the heavens or among humans can surpass her.
Adorned with celestial garments and necklaces that grace her body,
she has bracelets and bangles upon both wrists; her left hand is held upward, cradling a celestial flower,
while her right hand is held downward in the gesture of grasping the hem of her skirt.
The physical form may be three feet tall,
or one may take whatever size is appropriate according to one's own scale; once the image has been completed,
install it within the maṇḍala according to the ritual rules and make offerings.
Regarding the ritual for the altar of aspiration: the height of the altar should be four finger-widths, and its dimensions in cubits should correspond to the size of the location.
The altar is opened with four gates; inside the eastern gate, one burns agalloch incense.
Inside the southern gate, agarwood incense is burned;
at the western gate, frankincense is burned;
and at the northern gate, turushka incense is burned.
Place an image of the principal deity at the center of the mandala.
At the four corners, place a sword each and suspend a bright mirror.
At each of the four gates, two arrows must be placed.
On both sides of the southern gate, establish the positions for the Vināyakas.
Along the four edges of the maṇḍala, arrange sweet and succulent flowers,
fruits, and so forth, according to one’s capacity, as offerings.
Next, the ritual for the fire altar (*agnimaṇḍala*) is explained: construct a *homa* hearth twelve finger-widths deep, with a horizontal measurement of one cubit (*hasta*).
Beside the altar, fashion the form of that enemy.
Perform the homa with a knife while reciting the mantra;
use black tongs to pierce pieces of wood and burn various poisonous drugs,
burning one for each recitation of the vidyā.
If one recites it forty-nine or one hundred and eight times,
a great efficacy will manifest and those enemies will immediately be extinguished.
If one treats all diseases, it is also according to the method above.
One should fashion the forms of those spirits and ghosts, cut them up, and burn them; thus, fatal illnesses will be cured immediately.
This is the *dhāraṇī* seal for accomplishing the various arts and celestial maidens manifested through the supernatural transformations and playful emanations of Maheśvara, the Great Lord.
Join the two hands in *añjali*.
Cross the two index fingers and the two middle fingers externally,
with the surfaces of the fingers touching the backs of the hands.
Slightly curling the tips of the two index fingers so they resemble jewels, move the tips of the two thumbs back and forth together;
this constitutes the recitation for the mantra of invocation: [Insert Mantra Here]
Namo maheśvarāya uccairmukhāya īkṣasvāhā. Having tied this mudrā, [recite as follows].
Recite this mantra seven times to invoke the principal deity and all their retinues,
so that they may all descend and provide various kinds of empowerments and provisions.
Next, perform the seal for summoning all through supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
Straighten the middle finger of the right hand,
then place the ring finger behind the middle finger.
Hook the tips of the index fingers;
cross the thumbs over to press down on the second joints of the index fingers;
and extend the middle fingers outward in the shape of hooks.
The hook moves toward and away from the body;
this is the recitation of the root mantra.
To the word *svāhā*, one adds the name of the person to be summoned and thus invites them.
If one binds this mudrā and recites the mantra,
all will be summoned and arrive;
this is the mudrā for summoning through supernatural power.
It also functions universally in all places;
should one encounter a hostile or evil person who wishes to inflict harm or injury, [this practice shall protect].
Forming the mudrā, extend the middle fingers;
by pointing them toward those [demons], they will naturally disintegrate.
By pointing at various evil spirits and ghosts, they will be extinguished.
Having bound this mudrā and recited the root mantra,
seal the heart, forehead, throat, and crown of the head; thus one’s body is protected,
and no ghosts or demons will dare to approach.
This rite must necessarily be received through direct transmission from a master.
Having purified the chamber and secretly maintained the practice, once each recitation is completed,
cover the celestial image with clean silk cloth.
One must not rashly explain this Dharma to others;
if one should falsely divulge it,
it will remain ineffective for the rest of one's life.
Be careful, be careful!
Whether the celestial image is painted or made of plain silk, ensure it is complete.
Install the image of the principal deity at the center of the altar.
On the left and right of [the central deity], place two female deities (devīs).
If they are to be seated within the maṇḍala,
their forms and features should be pleasing.
The form is like that of a celestial maiden (*devī*).
Behind the image, two attendant female deities are further placed in their positions;
only the space in front is reserved for the location of the fire pit.
Burn various incense and medicinal herbs as offerings to one's tutelary deity.
If it is not possible to install a brazier,
place a single precious basin there instead.
It is also permissible to fill [vessels] with scented water and offer them adorned with various exquisite flowers.
Regarding the swords and arrows, if one is unable to place them at the four corners and four gates of the mandala,
it is sufficient to draw them outside the mandala.
Simply move the mirrors and place them at the four corners within the mandala,
according to the ritual procedures for other mandalas;
as for the location of the karma-vajra, it may be placed facing upward.
When painting the mandala,
one should depict five-colored rainbow clouds on the ground at the four sides of the mandala,
appearing as if they are supporting the mandala and leaping up from the earth.
The Rite of the Celestial Maiden Born from the Crown of Maheśvara’s Head
